articles.title: Arizona State's trip to London evokes memories of football in Tokyo
articles.summary: Arizona State football is playing in London on Sept. 19. Its last international trip was in 1990, and that game was quite the offensive showcase.
articles.body:
LONDON — One of the most memorable games in Arizona State football history came against Houston in 1990.

The highlight of that game, played in Tokyo, was a record-setting performance by Houston quarterback David Klingler, who threw for 716 yards and seven touchdowns. Paul Justin, the quarterback for ASU, threw for 474 yards. Houston won the game, then known as the Coca-Cola Classic, 62-45, and traditionally played in December after the regular season.

That annual showcase was played from 1977 to 1993, originally named the Mirage Bowl.

On Sept. 19, Coach Kenny Dillingham's Sun Devils (1-1) will face off against Kansas (1-1) at Wembley Stadium in London. This marks the longest road trip for ASU since that contest in which Klinger set a then-NCAA record.

Will this game, the Big 12 Conference opener for both teams, be just as memorable? Time will tell.

Arizona State football hits the road, takes on No. 9 Texas A&M

Tim Healey, the radio voice of the Sun Devils for the last 29 years, was on that trip in a different capacity. He didn't get the radio job until 1998, but he was the television play-by-play man for football and men's basketball games that aired on Channel 3.

Although that game was not televised, Healey still made the trip to Tokyo and recorded features all week for later use. He remembers it well. One thing of note: both teams flew on the same charter out of Los Angeles, something that would never happen nowadays.

"(Houston) had this run-and-shoot offense and just put up video game-like numbers," Healey said. "It was just crazy. We actually put up some really good numbers too, but we just couldn't quite keep up."

That trip to Tokyo and the current trip to London mark his only football endeavors outside the U.S.

Unlike the team, Healey actually returned to Arizona after the Texas A&M game, and flew back out on Tuesday, Sept. 15, with wife, Margie, arriving in London the next day.

He gives much of the credit for the preparation of the broadcast to producer Shawn Crespin, who is considered "essential personnel" and was on the team charter from Dallas to London.

Crespin had to weigh, label, and note the serial numbers of the equipment for documentation that comes with transporting products into a foreign country. Only the essentials were brought to London.

The team set up for the broadcast at the stadium on Friday, Sept. 18.

"The biggest thing was the conversion and making sure we were good there," Crespin said. "You connect with the venue, connect with the IT staff, and make sure you have everything you need. We've been working with them for months, so we were pretty well prepared."

This will be the first FBS game played on British soil. It is ASU's first game outside the continental United States since the 2006 Hawai'i Bowl and its second game outside the United States.

ASU also has a unique distinction in playing back-to-back road games, with one in an international setting. Arizona State is the first FBS team to play a true road game one week followed by an international game seven days later since Navy in 1996.

Healey expects the game to be right up there in his most memorable experiences.

"This is a forever thing. ASU and Kansas are playing the first game of college football in an iconic venue," he said. "American football has gotten more popular with all the NFL games being played over there. This is one of the most iconic venues in the world.

"I've gotten into Ted Lasso, and that gives you an idea of how the country views its 'football' and how passionate they are about it. Without question, it's going to be a memorable moment for the players and coaches, and all of us associated with this program."

articles.title: Oklahoma looks to continue impressive streak against New Mexico
articles.summary: Oklahoma is 2-0 against New Mexico, winning both meetings by shutout.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners will face the New Mexico Lobos on Saturday for the first time in more than 90 years. The Sooners and Lobos have faced off twice before.

The first meeting took place in 1930, with Oklahoma beating New Mexico 47-0. Oklahoma followed that up with a 25-0 win in 1935. That means the Sooners have an impressive shutout streak going against the Lobos.

However, it will not be easy to keep that streak alive, despite the Sooners having one of the best defenses in college football. New Mexico has the No. 21-ranked rushing attack at 246 yards per game. The Lobos also rank No. 7 in the country in scoring offense at 54 points per game.

The Sooners enter the game at 1-1 and are coming off their first loss of the season. The offense struggled in that game, losing to the Michigan Wolverines 17-10. They desperately need a bounce-back game.

The Lobos, meanwhile, are 2-0 with two blowout wins. The offense has put up big numbers, while the defense ranks No. 2 in the country in total defense. They pose a significant threat to the Sooners on Saturday.

Oklahoma's history against New Mexico may suggest a comfortable matchup, but the current Lobos are a completely different team. New Mexico won nine games last season and has won eight of its last nine games dating back to mid-2025. Under head coach Jason Eck, the Lobos have developed into a confident, well-coached team that has been determined on both sides of the ball this season.

That makes Saturday's game much more than a chance for Oklahoma to add another win to a decades-old series. The Sooners are coming off a loss, their offense has plenty to prove and New Mexico arrives in Norman with the production and confidence to make Oklahoma work for every possession.

The Sooners may have dominated this matchup nine decades ago, but none of that matters Saturday. If Oklahoma wants to leave Norman with a win, it will have to earn it against a New Mexico team that has every reason to believe it can pull off the upset.

articles.title: Dan’s Daily: ‘Canes Refuse Nikishin Trades? Malkin Future, Penguins Analysis
articles.summary: Evgeni Malkin may or may not be done playing hockey after this season, and he took a rather mature tone […]
articles.body:
Evgeni Malkin may or may not be done playing hockey after this season, and he took a rather mature tone on Friday. Not all of the Penguins seem happy about the glut of players, and one wonders if it's affecting camp. After a couple of days, trends and players who are on their game are emerging, including some of coach Dan Muse's early defensive pairings and potential line combinations.

Elsewhere in the Daily, it's got a Russian flavor. Alexander Nikishin 's agent shot down KHL rumors but essentially accused the Carolina Hurricanes of sitting on trades for his player. Ukrainian advocates are asking the NHL to sanction Alex Ovechkin . Kirill Marchenko had a good one-liner about his future, but is keeping mum on details. And Sportsnet asked the question—how will some of these long-term contracts age?

I have no stories, no more observations to share this morning. After I got home from camp around 5 p.m., I promptly handled some business, ate a hamburger with the crusts as buns because apparently I hadn't done any grocery shopping in over a week, and fell asleep by 7 p.m. Honestly, such a trivial annoyance as using the crusts made me laugh to myself. Life can't be too bad if that's the biggest annoyance, eh?

I am definitely not in hockey shape yet. But the eight hours were nice. So, let's do this hockey…

Pittsburgh Hockey Now: Evgeni Malkin . He either said, "I want to say yes" to playing another year, or "I won't say yes," but… It would mean the same. Malkin sounded a mature tone about his future and laid out the conditions under which he would want to play more years or retire. Evgeni Malkin held court .

What about Kris Letang ? Shelly Anderson had a chat with Letang and the future of the big three, too. Letang made a point of not being nostalgic about it .

Shells also talked with Filip Hallander about his future and what he's been through. Tell you what, Hallander looks pretty good in camp. Make no mistake, his journey and detour last season have made Hallander hungry .

PHN+: Two full days of observations and analysis, peppered with some of the conversations that I've had in the dressing room and reading between the lines. Come on back to PHN+—for a full accounting of Penguins training camp thoughts .

NHL Trade Talk, News, & National Hockey Now

NHLtraderumors.me: With some help from a Russian hockey writer, our buddy Dave Littman has the full story. Nikishin's agent indirectly blasted both Pierre LeBrun's report that Nikishin could return to the KHL and the Carolina Hurricanes for not trading Nikishin despite plenty of offers .

TSN: Ukrainian advocates aren't happy about Alex Ovechkin appearing in Vladimir Putin's political commercial and are asking the NHL to punish him for it .

We're in some real gray area here, aren't we? For the record, we have no plans to ask Malkin about any of this because, quite frankly, he's never taken a public stand. I don't know who tweeted it, but a media person suggested that if a player doesn't talk about politics, there's no reason to ask them about it. I like that standard. Ovechkin, however, has opened the door to being asked…

Sportsnet: The media giant referenced the Ville Koivunen contract as a bellwether, but didn't actually grade it. Instead, SN graded the deals that followed and which ones aren't going to age well .

The Athletic ($): Kirill Marchenko, the subject of so many trade rumors over the summer and reports that he won't sign in Columbus, did his preseason presser Friday. So, where does he want to play hockey? On the ice. Yep, he said it. Marchenko put on his tap shoes and danced around the hard questions but tried to be good to his teammates .

No, the Penguins can't steal Marchenko for merely second- and third-round picks, too.

Philly Hockey Now: Day 2 of Philly Flyers training camp. Will James has a good look at what's happening in Flyers camp .

Detroit Hockey Now: The lack of a GM in Detroit set contract negotiations back months with young defenseman Simon Edvinsson . But he's doing the team a solid and is in training camp without a new contract—but he had to sign a PTO?! Here's the scoop from Detroit Red Wings camp .

articles.title: Stephanie White divides Fever fans with controversial Caitlin Clark decision vs Tempo
articles.summary: A victory over the Toronto Tempo wasn’t enough to spare Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White from some fan criticism. Returning from the international br...
articles.body:
A victory over the Toronto Tempo wasn't enough to spare Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White from some fan criticism .

Returning from the international break, Stephanie White and the Indiana Fever didn't miss a beat, rolling to a 103-85 win over the Toronto Tempo.

Caitlin Clark picked up right where she left off, putting on a clinic in 34 minutes of action. She dropped 28 points, dished out 14 assists, and grabbed six rebounds, completely controlling the pace of the game. And that wasn't all, as Kelsey Mitchell broke the single-season WNBA scoring record with 33.

Stephanie White benches Caitlin Clark with 30 points and 10 assists on the line

Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White has had her fair share of critics this season, but it can be unwarranted at times – often being used as a scapegoat.

However, a decision during the Fever's win over the Toronto Tempo caused a bit of controversy, as White benched Caitlin Clark when she was two points away from another 30 pt and 10+ assists game.

This caused a complete divide on social media.

One supporter made a very valid point: "She played 34 minutes!! We cannot risk injury before our toughest stretch and playoffs for a measly 2 points."

Another pointed out how many minutes she played: "She played 33 minutes. I don't think she was as thinking about 30 with a game on Sunday."

"No coach in their right mind should risk a star player this close to playoffs to stat pad. Horrible uneducated take." Said one supporter.

On the flip side, some fans weren't too pleased.

Someone claimed that the Fever didn't want to take the shine off Kelsey Mitchell: "I noticed that. My first thought was they want to let Kelsey shine alone on breaking the most points record. Surely, that's not the case."

Another blamed White: "Stephanie loves messing with CC's game. Imagine what Clark could do under the right coach."

"As much as I hate it too, it ain't worth her getting hurt." This fan was split.

It's worth keeping in mind that Clark still logged 34 minutes after being listed as probable with a back issue. Plus, when Stephanie White pulled her late in the fourth, she cleared out the whole bench—it was just a routine line change to sit the starters, not a personal benching.

articles.title: “Why Are Girls Mad?” – Sophie Cunningham Shares a Hot Take on Sydney Sweeney’s Controversial Novig Ad
articles.summary: Sydney Sweeney stirred the sporting world with a controversial ad for Novig. The prediction-market platform’s latest featured The Housemaid star in the most...
articles.body:
Sydney Sweeney stirred the sporting world with a controversial ad for Novig. The prediction-market platform's latest featured The Housemaid star in the most illicit way possible. While most of the female athletes across different sports were outraged, Sophie Cunningham certainly had a more mature take on the ad.

In a recent episode of her No Hesitation podcast , featuring Drew Hanlen, the WNBA star questioned, "Why are girls mad?" Defending Sweeney, the WNBA star further said, "That is literally what she does. Why is anyone mad? It is a gambling ad. Men, sports, pretty much naked women. Of course that's going to draw attention."

Cunningham said that it was 'morally weird' for her to agree with the ad. However, she believed that the girls in sports were 'powerful and strong' and they portray what it meant to be an athlete.

"I don't think the ad was coming for women in sport," the Indiana Fever star said and continued her praise for female athletes. Cunningham added, "I think it has been so cool to see girls. They're muscly, their thighs touch, they have broad shoulders, they might be taller than the average girl and probably the average boy."

Sophie Cunningham Understands Why Sydney Sweeney's Latest Ad Is Drawing Backlash

The Euphoria actress staying in controversy with a controversial ad isn't a new thing. Even American Eagle's jeans ad garnered enough negative remarks across industries. However, it still managed to lift up the sales for the company.

With strategically placed sports equipment to hide nudity, the Euphoria actress kind of slayed in the new Novig ad . Since the release, female athletes have voiced against her not-so-appropriate involvement in sports.

Sophie Cunningham, on the other hand, believes the Novig ad has nothing to do with women in sports. Although she understands why the ad is stirring the pot, the Fever guard supports Sydney Sweeney.

"I can understand when you first see that ad; it kind of deflates women. Because we've worked so hard to get a little bit of respect around here, but then when you really think about it, it's like, screw it! Let that girl [Sweeney] go do her thing."

"We can still say this has nothing to do with us. So, you know, it's nothing like everyone trying to hate on each other and figure out life. So, that's great."

Sweeney's latest Novig ad saw her almost naked with football, basketball, golf clubs, and tennis racquets strategically hiding the nudity. The most controversial part of the ad was the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood actress constantly repeating the word "sports."

articles.title: 5 Questions with Arrowhead Pride: does Indy stand a chance?
articles.summary: In Week 2 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will hit the road to take on the Kansas City Chiefs. Knowing the party was headed to KC, I sat down with Maurice Els...
articles.body:
In Week 2 of 2026 our Indianapolis Colts will hit the road to take on the Kansas City Chiefs . Knowing the party was headed to KC, I sat down with Maurice Elston of Arrowhead Pride , SB Nation's Chiefs blog. You can find him on Twitter @MrMauriceElston . We swapped questions and answers about both the Chiefs and Colts and what follows is what I've learned about this week's opponent.

Chris Shepherd: Based on Week 1, if you were an offensive coordinator tasked with creating a game plan to attack the Chiefs' defense, what would your plan look like? What areas of the field would you attack, what weaknesses would you target and how would you try to beat this Chiefs defense?

Maurice Elston: I would do anything possible to force Kansas City 's linebackers—primarily Nick Bolton—to cover in space or match up one-on-one. Bolton is an excellent run defender and the commander of the Chiefs' defense, but operating in coverage over a large area is not his greatest strength.

I would attack the middle of the field with tight ends and running backs, using motion and different formations to create favorable matchups against the linebackers. The Colts have a tight end in Tyler Warren who is capable of presenting that type of problem. Getting Warren matched against Bolton or another linebacker in space could give Indianapolis an opportunity to consistently move the football.

Chris Shepherd: In Week 1, Colts fans watched in horror as the Ravens moved Zay Flowers all over the field to exploit favorable matchups that the discombobulated Colts secondary never figured out how to adjust to. Do you think the Chiefs will try to exploit those same issues, and if so, who will Andy Reid and Eric Bieniemy slot into the Zay Flowers role for Kansas City?

Maurice Elston: I don't believe the Chiefs will copy Baltimore's strategy exactly because Kansas City doesn't have to lean on one receiver the way the Ravens leaned on Flowers. I absolutely expect Andy Reid and Eric Bieniemy to test the same communication problems Indianapolis experienced in Week 1, but they will likely do it with several different players.

The Chiefs can use motion, shifts and formations to create favorable matchups for Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker III. Instead of putting one player in the Flowers role, Kansas City can force the Colts to identify and communicate against multiple threats before the snap. That unpredictability could make the assignment even more difficult for Indianapolis' secondary.

Chris Shepherd: In Week 1, Patrick Mahomes made his return after recovering from last season's torn ACL. He completed 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. Did Mahomes look like the Patrick of old? Was he still the player who can take over games, or will he need some time to regain that form?

Maurice Elston: I wouldn't say Mahomes completely looked like his old self, but he did look healthy—and that was the most important thing Kansas City needed to see.

Mahomes demonstrated that his knee is fine, he can still scramble and he remains capable of making plays outside the pocket. From a passing standpoint, however, there was some understandable rust. He opened the game completing only two of his first 12 attempts and missed a few routine throws that we normally see him make.

He eventually settled down and completed 13 of his final 15 attempts, including two touchdown passes. Because he couldn't participate in his normal offseason routine and did not play during the preseason, some early rust should have been expected. He may not be completely back to his old form yet, but the second half showed that he is getting there.

Chris Shepherd: Can you give me one player on offense and one on defense whom Colts fans might not be familiar with but who you expect to make an impact Sunday night?

Maurice Elston: Offensively, I would watch rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen. He became one of the Chiefs' most talked-about young players during training camp and the preseason. Allen received only one target and did not record a catch in Week 1, but I expect Kansas City to begin incorporating him into the offense.

In my opinion, Allen may already be the best pure route runner in the Chiefs' wide receiver room. His ability to separate could become especially valuable against the man-to-man coverage Kansas City's receivers have consistently faced.

Defensively, I'll go with L'Jarius Sneed. It may seem strange to call Sneed an under-the-radar player considering what he has accomplished, but much of the attention surrounding Kansas City's secondary has focused on young outside cornerbacks Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams.

Sneed's return to the slot gives Steve Spagnuolo a trusted defender who can cover, blitz and handle several different assignments. Having someone Spagnuolo trusts to lock down the slot changes what the Chiefs can do schematically, making Sneed an important piece of this defense even if he isn't receiving the most attention .

Chris Shepherd: How do you predict this game will play out? What does each team do well, where will they struggle and what is the final score?

Maurice Elston : I expect the Chiefs to win, although I don't anticipate the margin being as large as it was against Denver.

Indianapolis' best path to keeping the game close is through Jonathan Taylor and Tyler Warren. The Colts must remain committed to Taylor, stay ahead of the chains and use Warren to attack Kansas City's linebackers and safeties in coverage. There is no completely stopping Taylor because he is too talented, but if the Chiefs can contain him enough to force Indianapolis into third-and-long situations, Kansas City's pass rush and pressure packages can take control.

For the Colts defensively, the challenge will be handling Kansas City's motion, personnel groupings and improved running game without experiencing the communication breakdowns that hurt them against Baltimore. If those problems continue, Reid and Bieniemy will find ways to exploit them.

I believe Indianapolis keeps the game competitive for a while, but Kansas City eventually creates some separation and wins 24-14.

I can't thank Maurice enough for answering this week's questions. Make sure you head over to Arrowhead Pride and @MrMauriceElston on Twitter to check out his work.
